findings.title: SessionStart branch uses raw substring match, can swallow PreToolUse deny
findings.why_it_matters: run_hook_mode() dispatches on hook type by testing whether the literal substring "SessionStart" appears ANYWHERE in the raw stdin payload (case $payload in *SessionStart*)), not by extracting the `hook_event_name` field. For a real PreToolUse invocation, `$payload` is the full JSON blob including `tool_input.command` verbatim — so any Bash command whose text happens to contain the word "SessionStart" (e.g. a git commit whose message references the hook, or output being grepped/catted) makes this case match, causing the function to log "armed" and `return 0` *before* ever reaching the jq extraction, decide_command call, or deny emission. The mutating git command is never evaluated and is allowed to proceed silently. This is not a contrived adversarial input: this very repository's own commits, CONTRIBUTING.md, and this diff's files reference "SessionStart" constantly, so a routine commit such as `git -C /outside/tree commit -m "docs: wire SessionStart hook (mika#2107)"` would bypass the guard entirely — defeating the exact class of incident (mika#2107, four prior occurrences) this hook exists to stop.
evidence:
scripts/guard-shared-checkout:509-514: `case $payload in
*SessionStart*)
	guard_log "$GUARD_NAME: armed project=$(resolve_project_dir)"
	return 0
	;;
esac`

The match is a bash glob/substring test against the entire raw stdin payload, not a structured field read (no jq call precedes it); jq availability is only checked later at line 521, after this branch has already had the chance to return.

For PreToolUse, Claude Code's payload embeds `tool_input.command` verbatim inside the JSON, so any command text containing the token "SessionStart" makes the payload match `*SessionStart*` regardless of `hook_event_name`.

The adjacent `case $payload in *git*) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac` fast-path (lines ~516-519) is safe by contrast: absence of "git" anywhere in the payload genuinely proves the command cannot be a git invocation, so that shortcut has no false-negative direction. The SessionStart branch has no such soundness property — its false-positive direction is exactly a security bypass.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the fast-path check to the JSON key/value shape actually emitted for SessionStart payloads instead of a bare token, e.g. `case $payload in *'"hook_event_name":"SessionStart"'*)` (matching Claude Code's compact JSON encoding), or better, extract `hook_event_name` via jq once (`jq -r '.hook_event_name // empty' <<<"$payload"`) and branch on the exact value before doing any substring-based routing. Add a regression test asserting that a PreToolUse payload whose `tool_input.command` contains the literal string "SessionStart" is still evaluated by decide_command and can still deny.

residual_risks: Double-channel PreToolUse deny (scripts/guard-shared-checkout:558-563: writes `permissionDecisionReason` JSON to stdout via jq AND writes the reason to stderr AND returns exit code 2) is the author's own flagged uncertainty, documented in the 'DOUBLE CANAL' comment at lines 551-557 as an explicit bet that combining both channels can only be at least as blocking as either alone ('Aucun des deux ne peut être MOINS bloquant que l'autre'). External evidence gathered this review (WebSearch-synthesized, not primary-doc-confirmed — two closed GitHub issues, #43407 and #37210, both with zero comments and no maintainer confirmation) describes reports of the opposite: combining a JSON `permissionDecision:deny` payload with exit code 2 in the same PreToolUse hook invocation has been anecdotally associated with the deny being silently ignored and the tool call proceeding, on some Claude Code versions. This is unconfirmed and anchor-50 at best, but it directly undercuts the safety rationale for a fail-open security guard whose entire purpose is exactly this failure mode. Recommend an empirical probe — a live Claude Code session issuing a refused git command against this exact hook, confirmed blocked — before relying on the double-channel as the safety margin the comment claims; if disproven, prefer exit-code-2 alone (the better-attested channel) over the combination.

`.claude/settings.json`'s non-standard top-level `$comment` key (line 2, an array of French prose strings) is not validated against Claude Code's actual settings.json parser anywhere in this diff. Repo tooling (scripts/check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh) checks generic JSON validity and structural shape, not whether Claude Code's loader tolerates or rejects unknown top-level keys. Primary Anthropic docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks) were unreachable this session (WebFetch refused by this environment's tool policy on both attempts), so this is unconfirmed in either direction. If a stricter parser version ever rejects the whole file on an unrecognized key, both hooks (the PreToolUse deny and the SessionStart armed-proof) disappear together, silently, with no fallback — the exact failure mode the file's own prose (lines 16-18) claims is structurally impossible ('impossible d'avoir la garde sans la preuve qu'elle est chargée'). Recommend an empirical check that a live `claude` process loads this exact file without warning, or moving the rationale to a comment convention (if any) that Claude Code's settings loader is documented to explicitly support.

resolve_project_dir()'s production value of `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` inside dispatched pilot sessions (which of the two worktree-geometry levels — the meta worktree root `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` or the sub-repo `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/<sub-repo>` — it actually resolves to) was not confirmed from dispatch-lib.sh in this review; a grep for `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` there returned no match. The guard's own decision logic (path-containment check in decide_command, plus the on-disk-location fallback in resolve_project_dir) was verified correct for both possible geometries from code alone, so this residual risk affects confidence in which geometry occurs in practice, not correctness under either geometry.
testing_gaps: No test in this diff exercises a PreToolUse payload whose `tool_input.command` text contains the literal substring "SessionStart" — the exact input class that triggers the fail-open bypass described in the P0 finding above. scripts/test-guard-shared-checkout.sh should add a case asserting decide_command/run_hook_mode still evaluates and can still deny such a command.

scripts/test-guard-shared-checkout.sh exercises the double-channel deny output (exit 2 + JSON on stdout + reason on stderr) by invoking the script directly and inspecting its own output, which proves the script emits the documented contract but not that a live Claude Code process actually honors the deny when both channels are present together in one hook invocation — the exact combination the author's own code comment (lines 551-557) flags as unmeasured. No test in this diff drives an actual `claude` session through the hook end-to-end.
No test validates that Claude Code's settings.json loader accepts the non-standard `$comment` top-level key without rejecting or warning about the file.
